t:
Find the median of the following data. (Rounded off to 2 decimal places.)
Class interval | 0-5 | 5-10 | 10-15 | 15-20 | 20-25 | 25-30 | 30-35
Frequency | 3 | 5 | 4 | 2 | 7 | 6 | 5
e:
Total frequency (n): 3 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 7 + 6 + 5 = 32
Median position: (n/2) = 16th term
Cumulative frequencies:
0-5: 3
5-10: 8
10-15: 12
15-20: 14
20-25: 21
25-30: 27
30-35: 32
Median class: 20-25 (since 14 < 16 ≤ 21)
L = 20, F = 14, f = 7, c = 5
Median = L + ((n/2 - F) / f) X c
L- Lower limit of median class
F- Cummulative frequency
f- Freaquency of median class
c- class width
n- Total frequency.
= 20 + ((16 - 14) / 7) X 5
= 20 + (2/7) X 5
= 20 + 10/7 = 20 + 1.42857 = 21.42857
= 21.43
Option (a) is the correct answer.

t: In a seminar of 120 participants, 85 attended the morning session, 70 attended the afternoon session, and 20 attended neither. How many attended both sessions?
e: Number of participants attended at least one session = 120 - 20 = 100 Let A denotes the set of participants attended the morning session. And B denotes the set of participants attended the evening session. Using the formula, n(A B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B) 100 = 85 + 70 - n(A ∩ B) n(A ∩ B) = 155 - 100 n(A ∩ B) = 55 55 participants attended both sessions.

t: A person can hit a target 5 times out of 8 shots. If he fires 10 shots, what is the probability that he will hit the target twice?
e:
Probability of hitting the target P(H) = 5/8
Probability of not hitting the target P(H') = 1 - 5/8 = 3/8
If the person hit the target twice then he will not hit exactly 8 shots.
Probability that he will hit the target twice = <sup>10</sup>C<sub>2</sub> * [P(H)]<sup>2</sup> * [P(H')]<sup>8</sup>
= (10*9/2) * (5/8)<sup>2</sup> * (3/8)<sup>8</sup>
= 45 * 25 * 3<sup>8</sup>/8<sup>10</sup>
= (1125*3<sup>8</sup>)/8<sup>10</sup>
h: एक व्यक्ति 8 शॉट में से 5 बार लक्ष्य भेद सकता है। यदि वह 10 शॉट फायर करता है, तो उसके द्वारा लक्ष्य को दो बार भेदने की प्रायिकता कितनी है ?

t: In a class of 60 students, 38 passed in subject A and 52 passed in subject B. If every student passed in at least one subject, how many passed in both subjects?
e: Let A represents the set of students passed in subject A and B represents the set of students passed in subject B. Then, n(A) = 38, n(B) = 52 Since everybody passed in at least one subject, n(A B) = 60 Using the formula, n(A B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B) 60 = 38 + 52 - n(A ∩ B) n(A ∩ B) = 90 - 60 = 30
h: 60 विद्यार्थियों की एक कक्षा में, 38 विषय A में तथा 52 विषय B में उत्तीर्ण हुए। यदि प्रत्येक विद्यार्थी कम से कम एक विषय में उत्तीर्ण हुआ, तो कितने विद्यार्थी दोनों विषयों में उत्तीर्ण हुए?

t: At a conference of 150 attendees, 95 attended the morning workshop, 80 attended the evening workshop and 30 attended neither workshop. How many attendees attended only the evening workshop?
e: People who attended at least one workshop = 150 - 30 = 120 Using the formula, n(A B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B) At least one workshop = Morning + evening - Both 120 = 95 + 80 - Both Both = 175 - 120 = 55 Number of attendees attended only the evening workshop = Evening - Both = 80 - 55 = 25

t: Three cards are drawn one after another with replacement from a pack of cards. What is the probability of getting first card a Jack, second card a black card, and third card an even numbered card?
e:
Probability of drawing a Jack from a pack of cards = 4/52 = 1/13
Probability of drawing a black card from a pack of cards = 26/52 = 1/2
Probability of drawing an even numbered card from a pack of cards = 20/52 = 5/13
Required probability = 1/13 * ½ * 5/13
= 5/338

t: If set A = {4, 7, 6, 12, 18}, then for which of the following set B would A and B be disjoint sets?

e:
For two sets A and B to be disjoint, A ∩ B = φ.
So, B = {x: x is an even prime number} = {2} which is not an element of set A.
So, A and B are disjoint sets.
In option (a), A and B are not disjoint sets as all natural numbers are rational numbers.

t: In an online learning platform with 250 users, 140 enrolled in a coding course, 100 enrolled in a design course, and 70 enrolled in both courses. How many users did not enroll in either course?

t: The median of the data 40, 55, 50, 51, 72, 79, 68, 39, and 71 is X. If we replace 50 with 80, then the new median will be Y. Find the difference between the values of X and Y.
e:
Data in ascending order = 39, 40, 50, 51, 55, 68, 71, 72, and 79 = 9 terms
So, median (X) = 55
New data after replacing 50 with 80 = 39, 40, 51, 55, 68, 71, 72, 79, and 80
So, Median(Y) = 68
Required answer = 68 - 55 = 13

t: How many different arrangements of the word CREATION are possible, if they do not begin with OR?

Total number of ways = 8!
Total number of ways when they begin with OR = 6!
Total number of ways when they do not begin with OR = 8! - 6! = 55*6! = 39600

t: A speaks the truth 5 out of 7 times and B speaks truth 8 out of 9 times. What is the probability that they contradict each other in stating the same fact?
e:
P(A) = 5/7
P(B) = 8/9
Probability that A lies = 1-5/7 = 2/7
Probability that B lies = 1-8/9 = 1/9
Required probability = P(A) * P(B') + P(A') * P(B)
= (5/7) * (1/9) + (2/7) * (8/9)
= 5/63 + 16/63
= 21/63
= 1/3
h: A, 7 में से 5 बार सत्य बोलता है और B, 9 में से 8 बार सत्य बोलता है। उनके द्वारा समान तथ्य को कहने में एक दूसरे का खंडन करने की प्रायिकता कितनी है?

t: If the universal set U = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14}, set A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, and set B = {3, 6, 9, 12, 15}, then find the number of elements in set U - {A - B}.

In grade 11 of a school, 40 students opted for Physics, 17 opted for Biology, and 20 opted for Chemistry. If the total number of students in grade 11 was 60, all of these students opted for at least one of the three subjects mentioned here, and exactly five of these students opted for all these three subjects, what is the probability that a randomly selected student of grade 11 of this school would have opted for exactly one of these three subjects?
e:
Total number of students = 60
Number of students who opted two or more subjects = 40 + 17 + 20 + 5 - 60 = 12
Number of students who opted exactly one subject = 60 - 12 = 48
Probability = 48/60 = 0.8

t: Sudarsan and Abraham appear for an interview for two vacancies. The probability of Sudarsan's selection is 1/3 and that of Abraham's selection is 1/5. Find the probability that none of them be selected.
e:
Probability of Sudarsan's selection = 1/3
probability of Abraham's selection = 1/5
P(Sudarsan not selected) = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3
P(Abraham not selected) = 1 - 1/5 = 4/5
P(none) = 2/3 * 4/5 = 8/15
h: सुदर्शन और अब्राहम दो रिक्तियों के लिए साक्षात्कार के लिए उपस्थित होते हैं। सुदर्शन के चयन की संभावना 1/3 है और अब्राहम के चयन की संभावना 1/5 है। उनमें से किसी के भी चयनित न होने की संभावना ज्ञात कीजिए।

t: If the difference of the mode and median of a date is 41, then the difference of the median and mean is?
e:
Given that,
Mode - Median = 41
Mode = 41 + Median
We know that,
Mode = 3 x Median - 2 x Mean
41 + Median = 3 x Median - 2 x Mean
41 = 2 x Median - 2 x Mean

t: A die is cast thrice and a coin is tossed thrice. Find the probability that the die will turn a 3 each time and the coin will turn a head every time.
e:
The probability of coming 3 every time = 1/6 * 1/6 * 1/6 = 1/216
The probability of head every time = ½ * ½ * ½ = 1/8
Hence, the required probability = 1/216 * 1/8
= 1/1728
